entry.title: PACs — Dark Money and Felon Treasurers
entry.content:
Overview

Three political committees connected to the Banks network — two traditional PACs and one 501(c)(4) dark money organization. Convicted felons serve as treasurers and officers across all three.

Bank on Banks for Michigan

FieldValue
TreasurerJoseph Holland (drug trafficking conviction)
Total raised$22,225
Campaign finance fines$14,500+

Holland — a convicted drug offender (Controlled Substance — Possession) — serves as treasurer for this PAC while also holding Secretary and Treasurer positions at Purpose Foundation.

Bank on Wayne County

FieldValue
TreasurerBrian Roderick Banks (9 convictions)

Banks serves as treasurer for this Wayne County-focused political committee while simultaneously running charter schools and management companies in the same jurisdiction.

OFA Michigan (501(c)(4) Dark Money)

FieldValue
Type501(c)(4) social welfare organization
EIN87-2342269
AddressPO Box 361183
OfficerJoseph Holland

OFA Michigan operates as a dark money vehicle — funding political mailers without the disclosure requirements of traditional PACs. Holland serves as an officer.

entry.title: Billy McKinney — Political Operative
entry.content:
Position

FieldValue
NameDonavan “Billy” McKinney
TitleDetroit City Council Member (District 6)
ElectedNov 2021 special election (narrowly defeated Nicole Small, a Banks associate)
Sourcedetroitmi.gov, election records

McKinney occupies a seat on Detroit City Council, giving him vote on city contracts and budgets, oversight of city departments, and influence over District 6 — which includes Banks’ operational territory.

Connection to Banks Network — Darryl Banks 📄 Documented Jr.

TransactionAmountCycleSource
McKinney State House campaign → “Darryl Banks Jr.”$4,483 total2017–nowTransparencyUSA
Same campaign → “Darryl Banks Jr.”$2,2832024 cycleTransparencyUSA

A sitting Detroit City Council member’s campaign paid a Banks family member $4,483 total across cycles. The payment is classified as a disbursement (money out from campaign), not a donation.

Tier 1 Network Position

McKinney’s City Council seat provides:

  • Vote on city contracts and budgets
  • Oversight of city departments
  • Influence over District 6 including Banks’ operational territory
  • Political cover for the network’s city-level operations

The Banks network receives money from multiple political figures and campaigns, creating financial dependency. See Political Action Committees for cross-payment patterns including Inner Link Graphics ($98K+ from 7 network committees).
